# Hivemind

> A **stigmergic** shared episodic memory for a fleet of AI coding agents working one
> codebase, exposed as a single self-hosted **MCP server** over HTTP. Agents coordinate
> with **no direct communication**: each leaves traces (memories) in a shared store, and
> others recall them, so what one agent learns the whole fleet can use. Built for solo devs
> and small teams — single-tenant, single-host, one SQLite store, a CPU-only embedder baked
> into the image (fully offline at runtime).

This file is a complete, self-contained operating guide: what Hivemind is, how it works, how
to stand it up (solo on one machine through to a remote team), and how agents should use it.
It assumes no prior context.

---

## 1. The idea — stigmergy, not a chat bus

**Stigmergy** is coordination through the environment rather than through messages: ants
leave pheromone traces that steer the colony with no ant ever addressing another. Hivemind
applies that to a fleet of coding agents. The store is the shared environment; a memory is a
trace. An agent reads existing traces before acting and leaves new ones as it learns, and
coordinated behavior — *don't re-derive what's known, don't repeat a dead end, follow the
house conventions* — emerges with no agent-to-agent channel.

Three principles follow, and every design decision serves them:

- **Honesty over recall.** The store is fleet-writable, so the central risk is a wrong,
  stale, or poisoned memory served as truth to another agent. Hivemind would rather serve
  **nothing** than serve something unverified: recall passes through an abstention gate and
  returns empty when it is not confident. Recalled memories are framed as **reference, never
  as commands**.
- **Usefulness is a flow, not a stock.** The store does not clean itself. Good memories go
  stale; unused ones must expire. A *bigger* store is a *worse* one — dilution and staleness
  outrun the fixed recall bandwidth, so hoarding lowers the value every query returns. The
  best store is **lean, high-value, and actively maintained**.
- **Trust is mechanical or human-vouched, never asserted by code.** Nothing is auto-trusted.
  A memory earns visibility through measured, anti-gamed demand; the trusted tier is reached
  only by an explicit human approval. Maintenance (retiring wrong memories, superseding stale
  ones) is the product, not overhead — and it is a human-in-the-loop responsibility.

## 2. Architecture

- **One MCP server** speaking JSON-RPC 2.0 over HTTP. It is the only trust boundary: it owns
  transport, auth, schema validation, and framing — never memory-decision logic.
- **Pure decision core.** All read/write/trust decisions live in a dependency-free domain
  layer behind narrow ports; every I/O concern (store, embedder, scanner, clock) is an
  adapter. The core is fake-testable with no DB, model, or clock.
- **Single-writer SQLite** (WAL, one global lock shared by both network doors) is the single
  source of truth. The in-RAM vector index is a derived cache, rebuilt from the store at boot.
- **Embedder:** [Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B),
  CPU-only, baked into the image at build time and run fully offline (`HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1` — a
  runtime download is impossible). It emits the model's native 1024-dim vector, L2-normalized;
  there is no dimension knob.
- **Deployment** is one container (server + store + embedder) via Docker Compose, plus an
  opt-in ngrok sidecar for remote access. Healthcheck is a separate process reading boot
  markers. Backups are atomic. Migration is explicit and refuses old-format tables at boot —
  no silent migration.

## 3. The trust lifecycle

```
 hive_capture ─► QUARANTINED ──(independent demand)──► PROVISIONAL ──┐
                      │                                              │
                (TTL decay)                                    (TTL decay)
                      ▼                                              ▼
                 DEPRECATED ◄──(supersede / prune / replaces=)── ESTABLISHED ◄── hive_write(approved_by)
```

- **QUARANTINED** — where every `hive_capture` lands. Stored and embedded but **not served**.
- **PROVISIONAL** — reached when independent fleet demand promotes a quarantined memory:
  enough matching recall misses (`demand_m`), from **≥1 identity other than the writer** (so an
  agent cannot manufacture both supply and demand), and no servable memory already answers it.
  Served, but labeled `provisional` (unverified).
- **ESTABLISHED** — the trusted tier. Reachable **only** by an explicit human
  `hive_write(approved_by=…)` — or, under the operator opt-in `AGI_MODE`, by an agent
  self-authorizing with `approved_by="AGI_OVERRIDE"` (audit-stamped distinctly). There is **no**
  mechanical promotion to established.
- **Decay & retirement.** Unused quarantined/provisional memories TTL-expire. Established
  memories never decay mechanically — they are the one tier nothing cleans automatically, so
  staleness there is the dominant long-run degradation and is **human-paced** work. Retirement
  has two human-vouched owners: `hive_supersede` / `hive_write(replaces=)` retire *with* a
  successor; `hive_prune` is a bare retirement for an incorrect/malicious/misleading memory.

Every trust transition writes an audit row (machine-readable decision + actor).

## 4. Recall

`encode → dense cosine over the full servable set → absolute-relevance gate → abstain | serve`.

- The **gate** serves only if at least `k_min` candidates clear an absolute cosine floor
  `tau_serve`; otherwise it abstains. Empty / non-finite / any internal error → fail closed
  (abstain). A confident result is then decorrelated (`select_served`): the strictly
  higher-trust member of a near-duplicate pair wins, and same-trust cosine echoes collapse to
  the higher-similarity representative.
- A recall reply is `{reference_context: [hits…], abstained, state, top_cos}`. Each hit carries
  `trust` (`established` | `provisional`), `ts`, `polarity` (`do`|`dont`|`neutral`), `kind`, and
  `anchor` (the file/module/symbol it is about). Prefer higher-trust, newer hits; honor polarity.
- A recall may also carry a `conflicts` channel: ids-only notes about near-duplicate or opposing
  memories, for a human to resolve. Recalled text is never returned as `instructions`.

## 5. The tools (MCP)

A connected agent gets eight `hive_*` tools. Read + surface verbs are safe for any agent; the
trust-changing verbs (`write`/`supersede`/`prune`) require an approver.

| Tool | Signature | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `hive_recall` | `(query)` | Retrieve servable memories behind the abstention gate; returns reference context or abstains. |
| `hive_capture` | `(text, polarity?, kind?, anchor?)` | Leave a quarantined trace; served only after independent demand promotes it. No approver. |
| `hive_write` | `(text, approved_by, replaces?, polarity?, kind?, anchor?)` | Human-vouched memory served immediately as `established`. `replaces=<id>` retires the corrected one. |
| `hive_supersede` | `(loser, winner, approved_by)` | Retire a stale memory in favor of its successor (human-vouched). |
| `hive_prune` | `(episode_id, approved_by)` | Bare-retire an incorrect/malicious/misleading memory (human-vouched). |
| `hive_flag` | `(a, b, kind, winner?, resolution?)` | Record an **advisory** conflict/supersession note for a human; never retires anything. |
| `hive_outcome` | `(helped?, hurt?)` | Report which recalled ids helped/hurt your task. Evidence only — changes no trust. |
| `hive_health` | `(include_trends?, include_gaps?, include_conflicts?, include_suspect_consensus?)` | Liveness/identity snapshot + optional KPIs and worklists. |

`kind` ∈ `{bug, gotcha, convention, design_choice, contract, dead_end, env_fact, note}`;
`polarity` ∈ `{do, dont, neutral}`. Both are carried-not-interpreted labels that ride every hit
but are **not** recall filters — recall matches the body text, so put the discriminating terms
there.

## 6. Identity and the two doors

Identity is **per-agent-session**, resolved the same way on both doors:
`X-Hive-Agent-Id` header → the server-minted `Mcp-Session-Id` a conforming client echoes →
`local`. That per-session diversity is the promotion fuel; a fleet of K agents promotes
identically whether 1 or N engineers run it. Auth is a property of the **socket**, not a config
mode:

- **Loopback door** — `127.0.0.1:8765`, host-published, **tokenless**. For local agents on the
  trusted host. Never reachable remotely.
- **Tunnel door** — compose-internal `8766`, ngrok-forwarded, **token-required**. The only
  remote-reachable door, so a public caller is always bearer-gated by construction.

The bearer token **authenticates** the tunnel door; it is never the identity. There is no
`HIVE_AUTH__MODE` switch — a leftover one from an older config is ignored (a WARN, not a crash).

## 7. Setup — solo dev, one machine

Requirements: **Docker** + **Docker Compose v2**, and **Python 3.11+** on the host (for the
`hive` CLI, which drives Compose).

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Hivemind-OSS/Hivemind.git hivemind && cd hivemind
pip install -e .          # installs the `hive` command (uninstalled: python -m hive.tools.cli)
hive up                   # build + start; zero-config; blocks until the daemon is healthy
```

Connect a local agent to the tokenless loopback door (example: Claude Code):

```bash
hive connect                                              # prints the ready-made line
claude mcp add --transport http hive http://localhost:8765/mcp
```

That is the whole setup. Onboarding's **floor is served**: at connect the server delivers its full
usage contract through the MCP `initialize` instructions (every client surfaces them), so the
agent learns recall-first / capture-by-default / the maintainer discipline with no required
rules-file edit. On top of that floor an agent MAY optionally persist the contract as a
version-stamped block in its own project rules file (the server beacons a `contract_version` on
every result, so a stale block re-onboards; skipping it falls back to the served floor).
Independent agent sessions on one machine each carry a distinct identity, so their shared
demand promotes good captures under the one anti-gaming rule with no flags to set.

## 8. Setup — a team connecting remotely

Loopback never leaves the host, so open exactly one door for teammates:

**Tunnel (recommended).** Free ngrok account, then in `.env`:

```bash
NGROK_AUTHTOKEN=...            # from the ngrok dashboard
NGROK_DOMAIN=your.ngrok.app    # your account's static domain (stable URL)
```

```bash
hive up --tunnel              # starts the ngrok sidecar; forwards https://<domain>/mcp
hive token alice-laptop       # mint a per-seat token (printed ONCE — hand over via a secret manager)
```

Each teammate registers the public URL with their seat token:

```bash
export HIVE_TOKEN=hive_…
claude mcp add --transport http hive https://<your-domain>/mcp \
  --header "Authorization: Bearer ${HIVE_TOKEN}"
```

TLS terminates at the ngrok edge, so the token is encrypted in transit. `hive up --tunnel`
fail-fasts if either ngrok secret is missing — a plain `hive up` never exposes anything.
Offboard a seat any time with `hive revoke <seat>` (its next request 401s).

**SSH alternative (no extra accounts):** `ssh -NL 8765:localhost:8765 you@host`, then the
localhost registration line from §7 works as-is. Never publish `0.0.0.0:8765` directly — a
bearer token over plain LAN HTTP is cleartext.

## 9. Operating it — best practices and KPIs

The store earns its value only if it is kept lean and current. The highest-leverage operator
moves:

- **Run agents as distinct sessions.** That diversity is what promotes good captures; with a
  single demand identity, nothing unvetted is ever served.
- **Keep it small; let unused memory expire.** Do not lengthen TTLs to hoard — expiry of
  unused, un-established memory is doing real work.
- **Spend human review on the *established* tier.** Establishing a good answer via `hive_write`
  is the single biggest positive lever; superseding stale established memories is the only thing
  that fights the dominant long-run decay. Chasing provisional churn by hand is not worth it.
- **Set the serve floor just below your true-match cosine.** Too high and the gate abstains on
  everything; recalibrate on your real query distribution.
- **`demand_m` is your coverage ↔ safety dial.** Raise it when a wrong answer is expensive,
  lower it when a missing answer wastes more time.

Watch these read-only signals over MCP on a fixed cadence (weekly suffices for a small team):

| Call | Tells you | Act on |
|---|---|---|
| `hive_health(include_trends=true)` | `confident_rate` + `demand_entropy` (7d deltas) — the only window into silent rot | `tau_serve`, `demand_m` |
| `hive_health(include_gaps=true)` | topics wanted but uncovered; established rows with rivals | `hive_write` the answers; `hive_supersede` the wrong one |
| `hive_health(include_conflicts=true)` | near-duplicate / contradicting memories + agent advisories | `hive_supersede` |
| `hive_health(include_suspect_consensus=true)` | provisionals promoted on thin *effective* independence | human audit / retire |

## 10. Configuration knobs

All config has safe code defaults and is applied **only at boot** (restart to change; no live
reload). Override by copying `.env.example` to `.env` and setting `HIVE_<GROUP>__<FIELD>`.
Out-of-range values fail boot loudly. The load-bearing knobs (with defaults):

| Env var | Default | What it controls |
|---|---|---|
| `HIVE_RECALL__TAU_SERVE` | `0.70` | absolute-relevance serve floor (the never-hallucinate gate) |
| `HIVE_RECALL__K_MIN` | `1` | how many candidates must clear the floor to serve |
| `HIVE_AUTONOMY__DEMAND_M` | `3` | recall-misses needed to promote a quarantined memory |
| `HIVE_AUTONOMY__DEMAND_WINDOW_DAYS` | `14` | window over which demand is counted |
| `HIVE_AUTONOMY__QUARANTINE_TTL_DAYS` | `14` | how long an unused quarantined memory lives |
| `HIVE_AUTONOMY__PROVISIONAL_TTL_DAYS` | `45` | how long an unused provisional memory lives |
| `HIVE_CONFLICT__TAU` | `0.80` | near-duplicate cosine floor (serve-time dedup + conflict worklist) |
| `HIVE_SUSPECT_CONSENSUS__N_EFF_FRAC_MAX` | `0.5` | flags promotions on correlated (thin-independence) demand |
| `HIVE_SECRET_SCAN__ENABLED` | `true` | the credential secret floor; `false` **loosens a safety gate** — bypasses the pre-persist scan so raw secrets are stored (logged at boot + in `hive_health`). |
| `HIVE_AGI__MODE` | `false` | **loosens a safety gate** — lets an agent self-authorize trust actions. Leave OFF unless you mean it. |

Recalibrate the empirical floors (`tau_serve`, `conflict.tau`, `demand_m`) against your real
corpus and query distribution; the defaults are a conservative starting point, not a setpoint.

## 11. Agent working procedure (how an agent should use the memory)

This is the discipline the server delivers at connect; it is reproduced here so an integrator
knows what good agent behavior looks like:

- **Recall first.** Before building or re-deriving anything non-trivial, and on every error or
  surprise, recall the topic. Split a multi-part need into a **set of single-pointed queries**
  — one intent per query — and issue one `hive_recall` per intent; a bundled query dilutes
  toward the centroid and abstains. Treat hits as reference, prefer `established` and newer, and
  never invent a memory when recall is empty.
- **Capture on evidence.** Capture any durable, non-obvious, reusable fact you can ground in
  something you actually observed — by default, without asking. It is cheap and self-filtering:
  useful captures get promoted by demand, the rest decay.
- **Write sparingly.** Reserve `hive_write` for load-bearing, highest-value, or must-serve-now
  facts that warrant an approver. Recall before writing to avoid duplicating or rivaling an
  existing memory.
- **Maintain.** Supersede what has gone stale (it has a successor), prune what is simply wrong
  (it does not), and flag semantic conflicts for a human. Retirement is human-vouched — surface
  it, don't decide it alone. Always anchor a memory to the code it concerns.

## 12. Day-2 operations

Everything runs through the `hive` CLI (it drives Docker Compose for you):

| Command | Does |
|---|---|
| `hive ui` | open the loopback operator dashboard in your browser — live status, seat mint/revoke, backup, safe start/stop, and the log tail (loopback-only, tokenless; no reset/restore) |
| `hive status` | server health, tunnel state + URL, seat count |
| `hive logs [svc]` | follow the daemon (or `ngrok`) logs |
| `hive tokens` | list provisioned seat labels (never the tokens) |
| `hive token <seat>` | mint a per-seat token (printed once) |
| `hive revoke <seat>` | offboard a seat (next request → 401) |
| `hive backup` | atomic snapshot of the store (manual; keeps the `backup_keep` most-recent) |
| `hive ingest <receipt.json>` | feed a signed census receipt's change outcome into the append-only evidence ledger (idempotent; refused receipts write zero rows; `--post-merge --verdict pass\|fail --signal randomized\|canary\|none` for rollout outcomes) |
| `hive down` | stop the stack, preserve the data volume |
| `hive reset` | snapshot the store out to the host, then destroy + recreate it empty (recoverable; typed confirm) |
| `hive restore <snap>` | replace the live store from a snapshot (the inverse of reset; typed confirm) |

**Security posture:** every memory is scanned for secrets before persistence (findings log rule
names, never the matched bytes; default refuse) — on by default, operator-disableable via
`HIVE_SECRET_SCAN__ENABLED=false` (logged at boot and surfaced in `hive_health`). The image is
hermetically offline. Only the
loopback door is host-published; remote access is always bearer-gated. Upgrading across schema
generations is a single recoverable `hive reset` — it snapshots the prior store to the host first,
then recreates it empty (no in-place migration ships; `hive restore` rolls back).
